name: @thetis/bigquery
description: Google BigQuery as tools: list datasets and tables (date-sharded exports grouped), read schemas and preview rows for free, run SELECTs with a dry-run cost check and a per-query scan cap, run DML/DDL and scripts unless read-only, and follow jobs. Authenticates with a service account key or the space's gcloud login.

toolGroup.brief: Query Google BigQuery with SQL: datasets, table schemas, SELECT with cost checks, DML/DDL, jobs.

tools.name: bigquery_status
tools.description: Show what the bigquery_* tools run as: the account (service account or gcloud login), the project that runs and pays for queries, the default dataset, the per-query scan cap, read-only mode, and the datasets the account can see (which also proves the credential works). Call it first, and whenever a call fails on auth or permission.

tools.name: bigquery_datasets
tools.description: List the datasets in the project (id and location), or with `dataset` describe one: location, description, expirations, labels, its access list (who may read and write it) and how many tables it holds. Free; no query is run.

dataset.description: Describe this dataset (id or project.dataset) instead of listing.

search.description: Only datasets whose id contains this text.

project.description: Another project to look in, e.g. bigquery-public-data. Defaults to the package's project.

tools.name: bigquery_tables
tools.description: List the tables, views and materialized views in a dataset with their partitioning and clustering. Date-sharded tables (events_20260101, events_20260102, …, as the Google Analytics and Firebase exports write them) are grouped into one line `events_*` with the shard count and date range; query them as dataset.events_* filtered on _TABLE_SUFFIX. `sizes=true` adds row counts and sizes (one tiny metadata query). Otherwise free.

dataset.description: The dataset id (or project.dataset). Defaults to the package's `dataset` setting.

search.description: Only tables whose name contains this text.

sizes.description: Add row counts and storage size per table (and summed per shard group).

expand_shards.description: List every date shard on its own line instead of grouping them.

limit.description: Most lines to answer, 1-5000. Defaults to 300.

project.description: Another project to look in, e.g. bigquery-public-data. Defaults to the package's project.

tools.name: bigquery_table
tools.description: Describe one table, view or sharded table: its schema with nested RECORD fields indented and column descriptions, rows and size, partitioning and clustering (and whether queries must filter on the partition), and a view's SQL. `preview_rows` reads stored rows for free (tables only, no query, no ordering), optionally only `columns`. Read the schema here before writing SQL against a table; a name ending in * (events_*) shows the latest shard.

table.description: The table: dataset.table, project.dataset.table, or a bare name with `dataset` / the default dataset. A sharded table as events_* (the latest shard is shown).

dataset.description: The dataset id (or project.dataset). Defaults to the package's `dataset` setting.

project.description: Another project to look in, e.g. bigquery-public-data. Defaults to the package's project.

preview_rows.description: Also show this many stored rows, 0-100, read for free. Wide tables: name `columns`.

columns.description: With preview_rows: only these top-level columns (a list, or comma-separated).

format.description: How rows are written: `table` (default; one line per row, cells joined by |, nested values as JSON), `csv`, or `json` (an array of objects).

tools.name: bigquery_query
tools.description: Run one read-only GoogleSQL SELECT (standard SQL, not legacy) and answer the rows, the row count, the bytes scanned and billed with the on-demand cost, and the job id. It is dry-run first, free: anything that is not a SELECT is refused (use bigquery_execute), and so is a query that would scan more than the package's cap, with the estimate. `dry_run=true` answers only the estimate and the result columns. Cost is the bytes of the columns read, not the rows returned: LIMIT does not make a query cheaper; selecting fewer columns, filtering on the partition column, or narrowing _TABLE_SUFFIX on sharded tables does. Results are cached for 24 h, so a repeated query is free. Write table names in backticks with the dataset: `dataset.table`.

sql.description: One GoogleSQL SELECT statement (WITH … SELECT allowed).

dry_run.description: Only estimate: statement type, bytes it would scan and cost, tables it reads, result columns. Runs nothing.

use_cache.description: Use cached results when the same query ran in the last 24 hours. Defaults to true.

params.description: Named query parameters, referenced in the SQL as @name: {"day": "2026-01-01", "n": 10, "ids": [1, 2]}. Types are inferred (integer → INT64, number → FLOAT64, boolean → BOOL, list → ARRAY, else STRING); give {"type": "DATE", "value": "2026-01-01"} to name one. Prefer parameters to pasting values into the SQL.

dataset.description: Default dataset for unqualified table names in the SQL. Defaults to the package's `dataset` setting.

max_rows.description: Rows to return, 0-1000. Defaults to the package's maxRows (100). The rest stay readable with bigquery_job.

max_gb.description: Refuse if the dry run says it would scan more than this many GB. Can only lower the package's maxGbBilled cap, never raise it.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the result, 5-600. Defaults to the package's timeoutMs (60 s). A query still running then keeps running and is read with bigquery_job.

location.description: Job location (US, EU, a region) when it cannot be inferred from the tables, e.g. for INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

format.description: How rows are written: `table` (default; one line per row, cells joined by |, nested values as JSON), `csv`, or `json` (an array of objects).

tools.name: bigquery_execute
tools.description: Run a statement that changes data or schema: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, CREATE / ALTER / DROP (tables, views, functions), CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, TRUNCATE, or a multi-statement script. Answers the rows affected or the object created, the bytes billed and the job id, plus rows if the script ends in a SELECT. Dry-run first like bigquery_query and held to the same scan cap. Refused when the package is read-only, and by BigQuery when the account lacks write access to the dataset. Say what it will change before running it; DELETE, DROP and TRUNCATE cannot be undone (time travel can restore a table for 7 days: FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF).

dry_run.description: Only validate and estimate. Runs nothing.

params.description: Named query parameters, referenced in the SQL as @name: {"day": "2026-01-01", "n": 10, "ids": [1, 2]}. Types are inferred (integer → INT64, number → FLOAT64, boolean → BOOL, list → ARRAY, else STRING); give {"type": "DATE", "value": "2026-01-01"} to name one. Prefer parameters to pasting values into the SQL.

dataset.description: Default dataset for unqualified table names in the SQL. Defaults to the package's `dataset` setting.

max_rows.description: Rows to return, 0-1000. Defaults to the package's maxRows (100). The rest stay readable with bigquery_job.

max_gb.description: Refuse if the dry run says it would scan more than this many GB. Can only lower the package's maxGbBilled cap, never raise it.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the result, 5-600. Defaults to the package's timeoutMs (60 s). A query still running then keeps running and is read with bigquery_job.

location.description: Job location (US, EU, a region) when it cannot be inferred from the tables, e.g. for INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

format.description: How rows are written: `table` (default; one line per row, cells joined by |, nested values as JSON), `csv`, or `json` (an array of objects).

tools.name: bigquery_job
tools.description: Follow a query job: its state, who ran it, timings, bytes billed, SQL and error, and its result rows from `start_row` (to page past the first answer of bigquery_query, or read a query that outran its timeout). `wait_s` waits for a running job, `cancel=true` stops one. Without `job_id`, lists this account's recent jobs.

job_id.description: The job as bigquery_query printed it: project:LOCATION.job_id (a bare id works with `location`).

location.description: The job's location when job_id has none.

start_row.description: First result row to answer, from 0.

max_rows.description: Rows to answer, 0-1000. Defaults to the package's maxRows.

results.description: Answer result rows when the job is a finished query. Defaults to true.

wait_s.description: Wait up to this many seconds (0-600) for a running job to finish.

cancel.description: Ask BigQuery to cancel the job. It is billed for what it scanned before stopping.

state.description: Without job_id: only jobs in this state.

limit.description: Without job_id: how many recent jobs, 1-200. Defaults to 20.

format.description: How rows are written: `table` (default; one line per row, cells joined by |, nested values as JSON), `csv`, or `json` (an array of objects).

project.help: The Google Cloud project id that runs and pays for queries, and whose datasets are listed by default. Defaults to the project of the service account key.

credentialsJson.help: A service account key: the whole JSON file from IAM → Service accounts → Keys. Signed into a short-lived token here; the key never reaches the model. Give the account roles/bigquery.jobUser on the project, plus dataViewer (read) or dataEditor (write) on the datasets it should reach.

credentialFile.help: Instead of credentialsJson: the path of a service account key file in this space. With neither, the space's own gcloud login is used.

account.help: Only for the gcloud fallback: which of gcloud's credentialed accounts to use.

dataset.help: Default dataset: unqualified table names in SQL resolve to it, and bigquery_tables lists it when no dataset is named.

location.help: Job location (US, EU, or a region such as europe-west1). Unset: BigQuery infers it from the tables a query reads.

readOnly.help: When true, bigquery_execute refuses everything, so only SELECTs run. The real boundary is the account's IAM roles; this keeps the agent from trying.

maxGbBilled.help: Largest query to run, in GB scanned (10^9 bytes). Each query is dry-run first and refused above this, and the real run carries it as maximumBytesBilled so BigQuery stops it before billing. On-demand pricing is $6.25 per TiB, so 25 GB is at most about $0.14 a query.

maxRows.help: Rows a query answers by default (a call can ask for up to 1000). The rest stay readable with bigquery_job.

timeoutMs.help: How long a call waits for a query, in milliseconds (5000-600000). A query still running keeps running and is followed with bigquery_job.

maxChars.help: Longest answer a tool returns, in characters (2000-200000); longer ones are cut with a note that says how to narrow them.

apiUrl.help: BigQuery API base URL. Leave unset for Google's (https://bigquery.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2); set it for a proxy or an emulator.
